name: Origami filter membrane
subtitle: a membrane with pores of one exact size

effects.effect: DNA strands fold themselves into any designed nanoscale shape
small molecules seep through a membrane
a learned model predicts a protein's 3D shape from its sequence

effect: DNA strands fold themselves into any designed nanoscale shape
how: Filter membranes are made by casting plastic and hoping the holes come out roughly the same size, so they must be run at high pressure and still let some of the wrong things through. DNA strands can be written to fold themselves into a plate with a hole of an exact width, and billions of identical plates can be tiled onto a tough support. A filter whose every pore is the same size can separate at lower pressure, which is most of the cost of cleaning water.
obstacle: DNA plates are fragile in flowing water and in the salts and bleach a real plant uses.
why: Uniform pores would cut filtration energy; DNA's durability in service is the doubt.
real: DNA origami pores with exact apertures have been built and shown to span lipid membranes, conduct ions and pass water, and origami nanoplates have been laid over solid-state pores as size-selective lids, but two searches found no origami-pore array tiled into a working filtration or desalination membrane.
